payload.message: • Qualification: the ±0.031 is cross-validated on correlated samples. • That runs optimistic, per the GP error-quantification study (Xia et al., 2025). • Read it as a floor, not a ceiling.
Conclusion
• Confirmed: drag falls as the body grows; optimum at D=1.4 m, as hypothesised. • Monotone at every sampled point. • Improvement vs D=1 m baseline: +13.9%.
• Not confirmed: the predicted flattening near the bound. • Envelope 1.6% of value, wider than the gap between the last two designs. • Cannot separate them; claiming no curve shape unresolved.
• Still unknown: everything above Re 47. • Whether drag keeps falling needs an unsteady solver this study did not have.

payload.title: Cylinder shape optimization under a converged-solve constraint
abstract: We tested whether drag falls with body diameter over 0.7–1.4 m at fixed freestream conditions.
Across 5 solver runs the curve held and the optimum sat at the upper bound, D=1.4 m, improving on the baseline by 13.9%.
The reported value carries a 1.6% estimator envelope from a 12-sample ensemble; the predicted flattening near the bound remains unresolved.
methods: Two-dimensional steady laminar flow past a circular cylinder on a generated mesh, staged as calibration solver runs, a fitted reduced-order model, and gradient descent on the model.
5 solver runs; a reduced-order model calibrated on 4 solver runs carried the design gradient to the optimum, confirmed to within 0.0064 in drag coefficient.
Input uncertainty of 8% on freestream velocity propagated by a 12-sample Monte-Carlo ensemble.
Designs were admitted only if the solve converged and the case stayed inside the validated steady-laminar regime.

uncertainty: Estimator uncertainty is at least ±0.031 (1.6% of value) and is reducible: more samples narrow it as one over the square root of the count. Treat it as a floor rather than a bound; it is calibrated by cross-validation over design points that are correlated by construction, which is known to run optimistic.
Irreducible physical spread is ±0.11 at 95%, the stated freestream uncertainty propagating through the flow. No amount of sampling removes it.

Discretization error is not separated from either: the mesh was held fixed across designs, so it biases them together rather than changing the ranking. No grid refinement was run, so there is no numerical uncertainty to report at all.
